overall: Temperatures in Los Angeles have been essentially flat all morning, stuck at 62.6–63.0°F from before 06:00 ET through 08:52 ET with zero warming velocity — a hallmark of a persistent marine layer suppressing morning heating. The elevated dewpoint (57.2°F) and light southerly winds confirm onshore marine influence, which is running cooler than a typical June inland push would suggest. The day is behind the pace needed to reach model forecasts, but peak heating is still roughly 5 hours away.
forecast_obs_notes: NWP models cluster narrowly around 66.6–70.0°F (NBM 66.6, ECMWF 69.4, HRRR 70.0), showing reasonable agreement on the upper end near 69–70°F once the marine layer erodes. However, observed temps remain ~6–7°F below those targets at this hour with no measurable warming trend, and the intraday model's running max of 63.0°F reflects that suppression — the gap between obs-driven and NWP-based forecasts is notable and introduces downside risk to the NWS 69°F official call.
max_temp_prediction: The most reliable META bucket distribution centers probability mass around 68–75°F, with the highest individual bucket at 70–71°F (19.8%) and a broad secondary spread from 66–75°F. Given the flat morning trend and marine layer, there is modest downside risk of landing closer to 66–68°F if clouds linger past noon; however, partly sunny skies and ~5 hours of remaining heating time make a burn-off to 69–70°F the base case, consistent with NWS and the ECMWF/HRRR consensus. Confidence is moderate-low given high model entropy and the zero-velocity morning — ensemble signals recommend avoiding markets today due to wide uncertainty.
